title: WPSB/89/2003 of SANTOSH KUMAR CHANDOLA Vs ACCOUNTANT GENERAL and ORS

paras.text:
Writ Petition no.89 of 2003 (SB)
Santosh Kumar Chandola------- Petitioner
Versus
Accountant General, U.P. Allahabad and others ...... Respondents

Hon'ble M.M.Ghildiyal J.
Heard Sri C.D.Bahugana learned counsel for the petitioner and
Sri G.S.Bist, learned senior standing counsel for Union of India.
The petitioner by means of this writ petition has prayed for a
direction to respondents to pay penalized interest at the rate of 18 per cent
per annum on the amount of post retiral dues which were paid to him after
3/1/2 years. He has further prayed for payment of Rs.10,000.00 by way of
damages for causing harassment, humiliation and mental agony to the
petitioner and Rs.5000.00 towards miscellaneous expenses which the
petitioner had to incur during the period of more than 3/1/2 years.
The petitioner who was working as a head clerk in Industry
Department in district Pauri was retired from service on 31.03.1997. 90 per
cent of provident fund amount was released in favour of the petitioner by the
department though this amount was also released by the department after
eight months. However, he has confined his prayer only in respect of interest
on the amount which was paid by the Accountant General after 3/1/2 years
from his retirement. The learned counsel for the petitioner has drawn my
attention to the annexure 3 dated 14.3.2000 to the writ petition which is
sanction order of Account General, U.P. Allahabad releasing a sum of Rs.
36079.00 balance amount of G.P.F. to the petitioner. It is not disputed that
the petitioner was retired on 31.3.1997 and the 10 per cent amount of G.P.F.
was released by the Account General, U.P. Allahabad after three years.
Number of times learned counsel for the respondents was granted time to
file counter affidavit. On 11.6.2003 learned senior S.C. Government of India
was granted three weeks time to file counter affidavit. It was further clarified
in the order that no further time will be granted. Inspite of this no counter
affidavit has been filed. Today again he has sought further time to file
counter affidavit. The Learned Senior Standing Counsel Union of India has

submitted that under the rules the petitioner is entitled to 9% interest on
the amount which has been paid after three years. It is not disputed that the
petitioner was retired on 31.3.1997 and the Accountant General, U.P.
Allahabad has released 10 per cent of the amount of G.P.F. to the petitioner
only on 14.3.2000 after three years for which the petitioner is entitled to get
interest.
For the reasons stated above I direct the respondent no.1 to
pay to the petitioner the interest at the rate of 9% per cent on the amount of
Rs.36079.00 for a period of three years.
The writ petition is disposed of finally accordingly.
 (M.M.Ghildiyal J.)
July 17, 2003
MPS
